corrections.why: 18.3 m is 60 feet, the height a 1928 newspaper announced before the tower was built. The register describes the present tower as 29 feet 6 inches (about 9.0 m), and firelookout.com gives 28 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the first steel tower to 1928; firelookout.com says the site was established in 1932 with a 20-foot wooden L-4. The story uses 1928 and reports the 1932 claim.
The register says the 1928 tower was under 30 feet; newspapers of 1928 say 60 feet (April announcement) and 40 feet (June report). The story reports both.
Firelookout.com says the lookout is staffed by the Walker FPA; a Cheryl Hill index lists it as unmanned. The story gives both and does not settle it.

notes_for_editor: Record height 18.3 m appears to come from the 60-foot tower announced in 1928, not the present 29.5-foot tower; correction proposed. The 1928 tower's height and the first-lookout date are disputed in the sources. Staffing is contested (firelookout.com says staffed; a Cheryl Hill index says unmanned) and undated; check with Walker FPA or Fremont-Winema NF. Cheryl Hill's index also gives 1947 in the same row; that is not used. The register's 'Fremont National Forest' is now the Fremont-Winema NF. Access (whether the cab is open to visitors) is not stated in any source read. The 2003 registration date is from the register. A May 1941 newspaper item names a builder for the new tower; the register says the Forest Service constructed it, and the story follows the register.
